subject: Geography
sub_topic: Physiographic mapping — rivers, ranges, plateaus on outline map

concepts.name: Himalayan River Systems: Drainage Patterns and Antecedent Nature
key_dimensions: Antecedent vs consequent drainage — Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra predate Himalayan uplift
Gorge formation at syntaxial bends — Nanga Parbat (Indus) and Namcha Barwa (Brahmaputra)
Left vs right bank tributaries of Ganga — Yamuna, Ghaghra, Gandak, Kosi (right/left identification trap)
Transverse vs longitudinal valleys — Indus, Sutlej cutting across ranges

concepts.name: Peninsular River Systems: Eastward vs Westward Flowing Rivers
key_dimensions: Only westward-flowing major rivers: Narmada and Tapi — rift valley origin, no delta formation
Eastward-flowing rivers forming deltas: Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri — Bay of Bengal drainage
Western Ghats as watershed vs Eastern Ghats discontinuous nature
UPSC trap: Luni flows into Rann of Kutch (neither east nor west coast) — endorheic tendency

concepts.name: Indus River System: Course, Tributaries, and Treaty Significance
key_dimensions: Origin near Mansarovar (Tibet), enters India through Ladakh — mapping the entry point
Five rivers of Punjab: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej — left vs right bank identification
Indus Waters Treaty 1960: Eastern rivers to India, Western rivers to Pakistan
Shyok, Zanskar, Nubra — tributaries in Ladakh region frequently asked in map-based questions

concepts.name: Brahmaputra River System: Course Reversal and Tributary Identification
key_dimensions: Tsangpo (Tibet) → Siang (Arunachal) → Brahmaputra (Assam) — name changes along course
World's largest river island: Majuli — location in Assam on Brahmaputra
Left bank tributaries: Subansiri, Kameng, Manas, Sankosh vs right bank: Lohit, Dibang
Brahmaputra flows westward in Assam — counter-intuitive direction trap in map questions

concepts.name: Ganga River: Source, Tributaries, and Critical Confluences
key_dimensions: Gangotri glacier → Bhagirathi + Alaknanda meet at Devprayag = Ganga — Panch Prayag sequence
Right bank tributaries (Peninsular origin): Chambal, Betwa, Ken, Son, Damodar
Left bank tributaries (Himalayan origin): Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghra, Gandak, Kosi
UPSC trap: Yamuna joins at Prayagraj (right bank) — often confused as left bank

concepts.name: Deccan Plateau: Sub-divisions, Boundaries, and Physiographic Identity
key_dimensions: Bounded by Vindhyas (north), Western Ghats (west), Eastern Ghats (east) — triangular shape
Sub-divisions: Maharashtra Plateau, Karnataka Plateau, Telangana Plateau, Chhattisgarh Plain
Deccan Trap — lava plateau in Maharashtra/MP/Karnataka, distinct from Archaean Peninsular block
Highest point on Deccan: Anai Mudi (2695m) in Kerala — frequently misidentified as Western Ghats peak only

concepts.name: Western Ghats: Passes, Peaks, and Biogeographic Significance
key_dimensions: Major passes: Thal Ghat, Bhor Ghat (Maharashtra), Pal Ghat Gap (Kerala-Tamil Nadu) — transport routes
Highest peaks: Anai Mudi (Kerala), Doddabetta (Tamil Nadu) — state-wise peak identification
Pal Ghat Gap: only major break in Western Ghats — strategic and climatic significance
Western Ghats as UNESCO World Heritage — biodiversity hotspot, rain shadow effect on leeward side

concepts.name: Eastern Ghats: Discontinuous Nature, Ranges, and River Breaches
key_dimensions: Discontinuous ranges: Shevaroy, Javadi, Nallamala, Erramala, Mahendragiri — state-wise location
Rivers cutting through Eastern Ghats: Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri create gaps — unlike Western Ghats
Highest point: Jindhagada Peak (Andhra Pradesh) — often confused with Mahendragiri
Eastern vs Western Ghats: altitude, continuity, and rainfall interception comparison — UPSC comparison trap

concepts.name: Himalayan Ranges: Sequence and Parallel Zone Classification
key_dimensions: Four parallel zones S→N: Shiwaliks, Lesser Himalaya (Himachal), Greater Himalaya, Trans-Himalaya
Trans-Himalayan ranges: Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar — lie north of main Himalayan axis
Duns/Duars — longitudinal valleys between Shiwaliks and Lesser Himalayas: Dehradun, Patlidun
UPSC trap: Pir Panjal is in Lesser Himalaya (not Greater) — separates Kashmir Valley from Jammu

concepts.name: Trans-Himalayan Ranges: Karakoram, Ladakh, and Zaskar Identification
key_dimensions: Karakoram: highest range, K2 (8611m) — second highest peak in world, in PoK
Ladakh Range lies between Indus and Shyok rivers — separates Indus valley from Karakoram
Zaskar Range: southern boundary of Ladakh plateau — Zaskar River flows between Zaskar and Ladakh ranges
Siachen Glacier location — between Saltoro Ridge (Karakoram subsidiary) and main Karakoram

concepts.name: Vindhya and Satpura Ranges: Orientation, Rivers, and Structural Significance
key_dimensions: Vindhya: E-W orientation, northern escarpment of Deccan — historically northern limit of Deccan culture
Satpura: parallel to Vindhya, between Narmada (north) and Tapi (south) — horst block origin
Highest point in Satpura: Dhupgarh (Pachmarhi, MP) — often asked as highest point in MP
Narmada flows west in rift valley between Vindhya and Satpura — graben structure, not normal erosion

concepts.name: Aravalli Range: Age, Orientation, and Drainage Divide Role
key_dimensions: Oldest fold mountain in India — Precambrian origin, highly eroded
NE-SW orientation from Delhi (Raisina Hill) to Gujarat (Palanpur) — divides Thar and Gangetic drainage
Highest peak: Guru Shikhar (Mt. Abu, Rajasthan) — 1722m
UPSC trap: Aravallis act as watershed — west of Aravallis: Luni River (no outlet to sea), east: Chambal/Banas to Ganga

concepts.name: Northeastern Hill Ranges: Patkai, Naga, Mizo, and Meghalaya Plateau
key_dimensions: Purvanchal ranges: Patkai, Naga Hills, Manipur Hills, Mizo Hills — continuation of Arakan Yoma (Myanmar)
Meghalaya Plateau: detached block from Peninsula — Garo, Khasi, Jaintia Hills (W to E)
Highest peak in Northeast: Saramati (Nagaland) — often confused with peaks in Arunachal
Brahmaputra and Barak drain the region — Barak becomes Surma-Meghna in Bangladesh

concepts.name: Thar Desert and Luni River Basin: Drainage Anomalies
key_dimensions: Luni River: originates Pushkar (Aravallis), drains into Rann of Kutch — only significant river of Thar
Endorheic drainage in Thar — many rivers end in salt lakes (Sambhar, Didwana) not reaching sea
Sambhar Salt Lake: largest inland salt lake in India — tectonic origin, Rajasthan
UPSC trap: Luni is saline beyond Balotra town — lower course unfit for irrigation

concepts.name: Coastal Plains: Lagoons, Deltas, and Estuaries — Location Mapping
key_dimensions: East coast: wider, fertile deltaic plains — Chilika Lake (Odisha), Pulicat Lake (AP/Tamil Nadu) — lagoon identification
West coast: narrower, ria coasts — Vembanad Lake (Kerala), estuaries instead of deltas
Chilika: largest coastal lagoon in India, Pulicat: second largest — UPSC ranking trap
Narmada and Tapi form estuaries (not deltas) on west coast — structural/tectonic reason

concepts.name: Islands of India: Andaman-Nicobar and Lakshadweep — Physiographic Origin
key_dimensions: Andaman-Nicobar: submerged extension of Arakan Yoma (fold mountains) — volcanic origin at Barren and Narcondam
Lakshadweep: coral atolls — originated from Deccan Plateau submarine shelf, not volcanic
Ten Degree Channel: separates Andaman from Nicobar — Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from Lakshadweep
Indira Point (Great Nicobar): southernmost point of India — submerged partially in 2004 tsunami

concepts.name: River Interlinking and Inter-Basin Water Transfer — Physiographic Feasibility
key_dimensions: Ken-Betwa Link: first under NRLP — both Peninsular rivers, tributaries of Yamuna in Bundelkhand
Himalayan component: linking Ganga and Brahmaputra tributaries — surplus to deficit basins
Peninsular component: Mahanadi-Godavari-Krishna-Kaveri link — mapping the south-to-north flow reversal concept
UPSC trap: Godavari is surplus basin, Kaveri is deficit — interlinking direction and states involved

concepts.name: Chambal, Damodar, and Son Rivers: Peninsular Tributaries of Ganga — Identification Trap
key_dimensions: Chambal: originates Vindhyas (Mhow, MP), joins Yamuna in UP — notorious ravine terrain in MP/Rajasthan
Damodar: 'Sorrow of Bengal' — originates Jharkhand, joins Hooghly; DVC dams mapped here
Son: originates Amarkantak (shared with Narmada source) — flows NE to join Ganga near Patna
UPSC trap: Amarkantak is source of both Narmada (westward) and Son (eastward) — same plateau, opposite directions

concepts.name: Godavari River System: Course, Tributaries, and Delta Identification
key_dimensions: Largest Peninsular river — originates Trimbakeshwar (Nashik, Maharashtra), drains into Bay of Bengal
Major tributaries: Pranhita, Indravati, Maner (left bank — from Chhattisgarh/Telangana plateau)
Godavari delta: joint delta with Krishna — fertile, major rice-growing region of Andhra Pradesh
UPSC trap: Indravati (tributary of Godavari) flows through Bastar — Chitrakote Falls on Indravati, not Godavari

concepts.name: Plateau Regions of Central India: Malwa, Chhota Nagpur, and Meghalaya — Comparative Mapping
key_dimensions: Malwa Plateau: north of Vindhyas, drained by Chambal and Betwa — lava-capped, fertile black soil
Chhota Nagpur Plateau: ancient Archaean rocks, mineral-rich — Damodar valley coalfields, DMIC corridor
Meghalaya Plateau: separated from Peninsula by Garo-Rajmahal gap — Brahmaputra plain between them
UPSC trap: Rajmahal Hills (Jharkhand) and Garo Hills (Meghalaya) mark the gap separating Peninsula from Meghalaya block
